rationale: THE TWO MIXINS — the cross-file evidence the base-choice rule needs. Both are declared HERE, in a sibling file, so the project index is the only thing that can tell the analyzer which of them declares `onCheckForClose`. A single-file fixture could not exercise the rule at all: with the base and the member in one file, the per-file `exposed()` closure already answers, and the first-parent fallback never runs. The names are the MEASURED dart-http ones (`pkgs/http2/lib/src/error_handler.dart`), because a fixture that invents its own names measures a different thing. THE INDEX HALF of the fix is pinned by `script/m14/dart-override-mixin-base-check.ts`, which asserts that the project index NAMES both mixins and carries the right member sets — because the defect was that Dart's `mixin_declaration` has no `name` field, so the generic index read "" for every mixin and the spec "indexed the right SHAPE and held NOTHING" for the name.

forbidRelationships.note: A mixin does not override ITSELF. The base-choice rule is about a subclass's `@override` member, and a self-edge here would be a fabricated override.
the same for the second mixin.
